Bokony Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Bököny, Hungary

Not demolished. Bököny's Jewish community was founded by the Chief Rabbi of Nagykálló, making up roughly 5-6% of the village. The Orthodox synagogue, built around 120 years before this record, housed a Talmud school in its foyer at the village center. Population held near 190-197 from 1880-1910; by 1912, Judl Friedländer served as Chief Rabbi under community president Menyhért Kardos, supported by a four-member board and two-member supervisory board. By 1944, only 76 members remained (13 taxpayers), led by caretaker Menyhért Goldstein under Registrar Rabbi József Rosenfeld; the Chevra Kadisha's 12 members owned both the cemetery watchman's house and 1.24 acres of land. This cemetery's oldest tombstone dates to 1842, its newest to 1942. The Heritage Foundation for Preservation of Jewish Cemeteries fenced the site and erected a Holocaust memorial in 2002.
